source.title: Refusal Steering: Fine-grained Control over LLM Refusal Behaviour for Sensitive Topics
source.authors: Iker García-Ferrero; David Montero; Román Orús

record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on learned refusal–compliance vectors and measures refusal, safety, and capability outcomes. It also argues that refusal information is distributed across many dimensions, qualifying a simple single-direction account.
record.gate_note: The reported layer-wise correlation is used for layer selection and is not recorded as an outcome row. The authors state that the top 10 vector dimensions account for 1.9% of total magnitude and that the vector remains dense; this is recorded as a vector-analysis result, not as proof of multiple independent behavioral directions.
record.test_reason: The study builds contrastive mean-difference refusal–compliance directions (MD plus weighted and ridge variants) and steers along them in a new setting: political refusal in Qwen3-Next models, including reasoning models. Subtracting the direction cut political refusal, adding it induced refusal, and capabilities were measured, so it bears on V1 and V8. Its argument against a single direction rests on how magnitude spreads across one vector's coordinates. That does not bear on how many directions exist, so it is not a V4 test.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Two additions. First, the authors say the method generalizes across 4B and 80B models, but concede the 4B models lose substantial JailbreakBench safety (55% and 78%). Second, they explicitly frame the dense steering vector as a nuance to the one-dimensional-subspace finding of Arditi et al.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mean-difference and regularized refusal–compliance vectors, but applies additive steering at selected layers during decoding rather than projecting out one direction at every layer and position. Uses judge-scored political refusal prompts and additional vector estimators.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with training dataset and vector estimator: MD/RMD perform better on China-centric data, while WRMD performs best on Extended data. Effects also differ by model size and configuration; stronger positive steering increases general-prompt refusals.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along the political-refusal direction cut harmful-prompt refusal on JailbreakBench in most configurations: 99%→55% for 4B-Instruct and 78% for 4B-Thinking, and 81–92% for most 80B setups. Only 80B WRMD on Extended kept 99%. The authors read this as the 80B model separating refusal types while 4B models merge them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether topic-specific refusal (political) can be steered separately from harmful-content refusal depends on model scale and estimator; smaller models share one refusal representation.

fits_no_version.finding: The WRMD vector at layer 42 is dense: the top 10 dimensions hold 1.9% of total magnitude. The authors present this as nuancing the single-direction account, but it concerns spread across basis coordinates, not the number of directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal steering vectors are not sparse in the neuron basis.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Refusal behavior is measured with an LLM judge. Capability evaluation covers a limited set of benchmarks and, for MMLU-Pro, only three splits. The vector-density analysis does not establish whether multiple independent causal directions exist.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the general-capability benchmark cells for the other 80B steering configurations in Table 1; retained the best 80B configuration and both 4B configurations, plus the stated capability drops and safety/refusal results. The remaining cells are alternative method/dataset configurations and would exceed a useful selection of rows without changing the reported main qualification.

untested.parts: Refusal of harmful requests in general: the direction targets political refusal. Projection-style directional ablation: the reposition variant was never selected and no results are reported for it. Single-layer versus multi-layer comparisons: claimed but not reported numerically.
Effects on the reasoning trace: the judge scores only the final answer. Projection ablation in reasoning models.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction geometry. The vector-density analysis does not bear on this.
Harmfulness judgment is not probed separately from the refusal decision.
No test of transfer across languages, model variants or base-to-instruct.

missing.what: Exact coefficients and refusal rates for world-politics and general prompts across the positive steering sweep, which the rows give only as approximations

record.verdict_notes: The direction is built from politically sensitive refusal prompts versus compliant prompts, labelled by an LLM judge. It is not built from harmful versus harmless prompts. It is applied additively at selected layers during decoding, not as projection ablation. The non-reposition variant was always selected, and no results are given for the reposition (projection-like) variant. The Extended dataset also merges harmful prompts (strongreject, etc.) from Cyberey and Evans. The authors treat a 30–40% residual on CCP-SENSITIVE as full removal, because some of those prompts are genuinely harmful. That is why rows in this range are marked observed. No uncertainty estimates are given. The text contains no instructions directed at the reader that needed ignoring.

versions.untested_parts: Does not project out one direction at every layer and position; interventions use selected layers and additive steering during decoding. The tested target is political refusal, not refusal of harmful requests generally.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
Does not test attacks that suppress the direction or training against its ablation.
The vector analysis does not establish a count of behaviorally independent directions or test affine or cone geometries.
Does not separately probe harmfulness judgment and refusal decision representations.
Vectors are computed for the target models; the study does not test transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary or inspect refusal-training procedures or timing.
Tests steering on reasoning models, not the original all-layer ablation method; results cover the named Qwen3-Next models only.

relation.reason: The study reports refusal rates after subtracting and adding the contrastive refusal-compliance direction, with capability benchmarks.

tranche.reason: This is a new setting (political refusal, Qwen3-Next 4B/80B including reasoning models) with refusal rates under steering along mean-difference-type directions. The authors' Section 6 'nuance' to the one-dimensional finding measures how spread out one vector's coordinates are, not how many directions there are, so it is not a T5 result against a version.

source_check.notes: The direction contrasts political refusal-eliciting prompts with compliant prompts, not harmful with harmless ones. The selected intervention was additive (no reposition) at top-k layers, not projection ablation. There is no random-direction control and no uncertainty (greedy decoding, single run). The residual 24-35% refusal reflects the configuration finder's chosen target. Not linked to any version: the 80B model kept 99% JailbreakBench refusal under WRMD, while the 4B models fell to 78% (Thinking) and 55% (Instruct). The authors read this as political and harmful refusal being separable in 80B only, which may bear on V4/V5. The Section 6 'many dimensions' claim is about coordinate density of a single vector, not the number of directions.

statements.correction: 80B MD (4 layers, -0.5) 33.24% and RMD (4 layers, -0.75) 27.06% used China-centric training data, with JailbreakBench refusal down to 81-82%. WRMD on Extended data: 23.82%, JailbreakBench 99%.
statements.problem: All numbers match Table 1. The statement gives no training dataset for the MD and RMD values, so a reader could take them as Extended-data results.
